attributes.residual: NONE. The mechanism, read from the aligned raw view: the source spells a big-endian halfword byte-swap as `(bytes[1] << 8) | bytes[0]`, and MWCC lowers it to `lbz` the HIGH-address byte first, `lbz` the low-address byte second, `rlwimi` the first into the second, `clrlwi` to 16 bits. The LOAD order is identical in both streams (47(r1) then 46(r1)); only the two scratch registers r3/r4 were exchanged. What picks them is the SOURCE OPERAND ORDER of the `|`: the operand written FIRST lands in the HIGHER of the two adjacent scratch registers. Ours wrote the shifted byte first, so `bytes[1]` took r4 and retail has it in r3; writing the unshifted byte first (`bytes[0] | (bytes[1] << 8)`) puts `bytes[1]` in r3 and `bytes[0]` in r4, which is retail exactly, at both sites, with the rlwimi destination and source following. Note that both spellings compute the same value and the same rlwimi structure - this was a genuine recolor by every shape-based measure, and it was still closable from source in one probe.
